# link_target { #crossrepo.gitutil.link_target }

```python
crossrepo.gitutil.link_target(repo, blob_sha)
```

Read where a committed symbolic link points.

A symbolic link is stored as a blob whose content is the target path, so
this is the committed target rather than whatever the working tree happens
to hold, which is the same rule manifests are read by.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**repo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[Location](`crossrepo.location.Location`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`), [str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Working tree holding the blob, on this machine or another.

<code>[**blob_sha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Blob sha of the link, as `tracked_entries` reports it for a path whose mode is `LINK_MODE`.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The target as written, which may be relative to the directory the link sits in.
